content.text: iVH’s engineering was not created with a single industry in mind.
**We have accumulated a common engineering foundation over a long period,**
and as a result, it has been implemented as various types of systems across diverse industrial sectors.
While the fields of Mobility, Manufacturing, Energy, and Building may appear to be entirely different industries on the surface,
to iVH, they are **all system-level challenges where physical systems, control, operation, and verification are integrated.**

blocks.title: Future Mobility
blocks.subtitle: Engineering Intelligent, Verifiable, and Expandable Mobility Systems

content.text: Future mobility systems are no longer completed by mechanical performance or individual control technologies alone.
Sensors, controllers, software, environments, and operational scenarios must be designed and verified as a single integrated system.
iVH has pioneered the domestic application of **Modelica-based system engineering and ASAM-based verification frameworks,** focusing on the automotive industry.

content.label: Key Engineering Approaches
items: Structural modeling of vehicle and mobility systems
Construction of scenario-based virtual test environments
System V&V integrating controllers, environments, and sensors
Verification processes reflecting real-world road and operational conditions

content.label: Representative Application Cases
items: Development of verification platforms for autonomous driving and ADAS systems
Establishment of evaluation systems linking real-vehicle data with simulation environments
Standardization of V&V-centered development processes for domestic companies

content.text: These experiences are extending beyond traditional vehicles to special-purpose vehicles, robot-based mobility, and in-factory transportation systems.

blocks.title: Smart Factory & Logistics
blocks.subtitle: Engineering Operable Factories, Not Just Automated Equipment

content.text: Many factories already possess automated equipment.
However, factories where operations judge and adjust on their own are rare.
iVH views a factory not as a collection of individual automated devices,
but **as a single System of Systems.**

content.label: Key Engineering Approaches
items: System modeling of factory logistics flows
Structural design integrating AMRs, collaborative robots, equipment, and MES
Verification of process and logistics scenarios based on Digital Twins
Operational optimization including real-time judgment and re-planning through Physical AI

content.label: Representative Development and Application Cases
items: Development of AMR and collaborative robot-integrated logistics systems for manufacturing processes
Control and scheduling systems for simultaneous operation of multiple robots
Advancement of Physical AI-integrated control functions based on process context awareness
Field verification and application at domestic automotive parts manufacturing sites

content.text: iVH goes beyond simple transportation automation to **implement intelligent logistics systems that perceive and coordinate the entire process** in actual field environments.

blocks.title: Energy Systems
blocks.subtitle: Engineering Integrated and Hybrid Energy Systems

content.text: The core issue in the energy sectoris not the efficiency of a single facility,
but **the interactions between systems and their operational strategies.**
iVH has long treated energy not as "power generation equipment" but as **an operable energy system.**

content.label: Key Engineering Approaches
items: Integrated system modeling of SMRs, renewable energy, power grids, and ESS
Construction of Modelica-based multi-physics Energy System Digital Twins
Verification of operational scenarios considering load, storage, and control
System optimization from the perspectives of economics, stability, and flexibility

content.label: Representative Development and Application Cases
items: Modeling and verification of NR-HES (Nuclear-Renewable Hybrid Energy Systems)
Research on SMR load-following and ESS-connected operational scenarios
Analysis of power grid stability and energy storage strategies
Energy system controller verification and establishment of V&V environments

content.text: These engineering experiences are **extending beyond simple power production to future energy operating systems.**

blocks.title: Engineering Energy at the Operational Scale

content.text: Building Energy Management is a representative field **where energy system engineering is implemented at the site level.**
iVH has modeled buildings as single energy systems and applied **Engineering Digital Twin + Physical AI** that can be used for actual decision-making during the operational phase.

content.label: Key Engineering Approaches
items: Construction of BIM-based Building Digital Twins
Integrated modeling of HVAC, power, and ESS
Continuous updates of models reflecting operational data
Physical AI-based energy operation, control, and anomaly diagnosis

content.label: Representative Development and Application Cases
items: Establishment of a BIM–Digital Twin–BEMS connection pipeline
Development of a building energy operation optimization simulator
Physical AI-based building O&M decision-making system
Verification of energy savings through application to demonstration buildings

content.text: BEMS is the interface where **iVH’s energy system engineering and Physical AI are integrated within a real-world operational environment.**
One Engineering, Multiple Industries
iVH is not a company that creates new technologies for each industry on the fly.
We have expanded across industries based on:

items: A single System Engineering philosophy
A common foundation of Modelica, ASAM, and Physical AI
Verified experiences accumulated through field applications

content.text:
Same Engineering,
Different Industries,
And continuously evolving domains of application.
This is iVH’s **Engineering to Industry** approach.
